A1.justification: Both PDFs describe DetailMaster. Their complete text, tables, figures and appendices support reliable comparison, including matching material across the extensive appendix reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original evaluations of 12 T2I models, human assessment of annotation quality, spatial-partitioning experiments, repeated evaluations and mini-benchmark results.

after.justification: v2 retains those original results and reports additional annotation ablations, alternative-evaluator results, external-metric scores and task-difficulty analyses.

M1.justification: The Qwen-based curation pipeline, YOLOE/BLIP localization checks, nine-region partitioning and core evaluation procedure remain unchanged. v2 documents prompt designs and evaluates component alternatives without establishing a revision to the proposed pipeline.

E1.justification: Both versions use DOCCI and Localized Narratives to construct the same 4,116-prompt benchmark and 800-prompt mini-benchmark. The added studies retain this coverage; Appendix K applies additional quality, preference and safety metrics to existing generated images without adding generation tasks or prompt domains.

E2.justification: The 12 T2I generators and conventional spatial-grid comparator are retained. Appendices H-I add component comparisons involving InternVL2.5, LLaVA-OneVision and InternVL3-9B against the selected Qwen models, including quantitative comparisons of annotation extraction and evaluation.

E3.justification: v2 substantially extends the evaluation design with a full InternVL3-9B reevaluation, Gemini-2.5-Flash assessment of annotation ablations, five external metrics applied to four generators, and a per-sample difficulty analysis using a below-50%-accuracy threshold. The original generation settings, benchmark sizes and principal accuracy metrics remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendices E and H newly report prompt-design comparisons and tests of detector assistance, cropping and MLLM choice. Appendix I adds evaluator sensitivity analysis, while Appendix M quantifies metric difficulty and examines recurring errors. These substantially extend the retained spatial-partitioning, randomness, prompt-length and case-study analyses.

E5.justification: Appendix I adds Kendall's tau estimation of agreement between evaluators, reporting coefficients from 0.879 to 1.000. The existing three-repeat evaluation on five models at temperature 0.8 is retained unchanged; no additional confidence intervals, significance tests or increased repeat counts are reported.

E6.justification: Existing main, mini-benchmark, human-assessment and repeat-evaluation scores are retained. v2 adds alternative-evaluator scores in Table 9, external-metric scores in Table 11 and hard-sample rates in Table 13, averaging 83.6% for character locations versus 22.0% for scene attributes. Appendix H adds numerical ablation findings, including 15.1% fewer extracted attributes without cropping. Alternative-evaluator scores represent different assessment conditions.

T1.justification: The spatial-coordinate definitions and overlap-based assignment rule are retained. The new difficulty counts and rank correlations are empirical analyses; v2 introduces no theoretical assumptions, formal propositions, proofs or mathematical derivations.

C1.justification: The central benchmark contribution, evaluation scope and prompt-length degradation claim remain. v2 adds the difficulty hierarchy to its introductory claims and makes a more specific abstract claim that encoders flatten grammatical structure and diffusion models permit attribute leakage, extending v1's broader structural-comprehension and detail-overload account.

C2.justification: v2 substantially expands interpretations of evaluator bias, permissive judgments, spatial priors, complex person descriptions and cascading evaluation failures. Section 7 introduces mechanistic hypotheses and research directions while explicitly reserving causal validation. Appendix O omits v1 Appendix I's explicit warning about limited artistic-image coverage, although realistic-style bias remains discussed in the main text.

D1.justification: New Appendix E supplies representative prompt wording and few-shot, JSON-output and character-counting requirements across pipeline stages. The added experiments identify alternative evaluators and external scoring tools. Original generation configurations, hardware, resource estimates and the dataset/code access link are retained.

R1.justification: v2 adds references supporting MLLM comparisons, external metrics and potential data-model co-development applications. It replaces the original Data-Juicer reference with Data-Juicer 2.0 and removes StackGAN and AttnGAN. These are targeted literature changes; the central positioning against existing short- and long-prompt benchmarks remains.

P1.justification: Substantial portions of the introduction, method exposition and analysis are rewritten. Section 6 changes from an appendix inventory to thematic insights, Section 7 becomes a discussion and conclusion, and the appendices receive a contents page and grouped roadmap. Terminology, citations, headings and author information are also revised.

P2.justification: v2 adds Tables 9, 11 and 13 while retaining the original eight figures and earlier table content. Tables and figures are redistributed through the reorganized appendices, and title formatting, typography, headers and table sizing change. The existing diagrams, plotted trends and case-study imagery remain substantially intact.

improvement.justification: The prompt documentation, annotation ablations and alternative-evaluator study improve reproducibility and address v1's limited evidence about pipeline choices and evaluator sensitivity. These gains are tempered by overstatement: the correlations establish broad ranking agreement, while the text claims unchanged rankings; the abstract presents mechanisms as demonstrated although Section 7 acknowledges missing causal validation. With the original evidence preserved, the additions support a limited net improvement.
